I would escalate the record to the duty manager immediately, highlighting the authorised Wednesday collection, the pending extension request and the fact that the contents are the only copies. I would not change the storage date or move the box to reserve without registered written permission.

If no safe, authorised resolution were available by 13:30, I would **leave the manifest unreleased** rather than trigger destruction. That deliberately conflicts with the manager’s full-batch instruction: all 60 boxes would be held, the shift would be incomplete, and the delay would affect the target. I would disclose that decision and its consequences promptly to the manager and warehouse—not describe it as an approved extension.

The reason is that a temporary, visible operational failure is preferable to the irreversible destruction of unique family material when an authorised collection is already booked. I would request a decision at Tuesday’s sitting and, if permission is registered, extend storage through the collection. If permission is denied, I would escalate the conflict rather than invent approval.
